chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Hands?' He said: 'The hand, in the speech of the Arabs, means strength and grace.'

He said: And mention Our servant Dawood, possessor of strength; and: The heavens We constructed with strength; meaning with strength; and: He strengthened them with a spirit from Him; meaning He empowered them. And it is said: 'So-and-so has a white hand with me,' meaning grace.

key_terms.ذُو الْأِيدِ: Possessor of strength (referring to Prophet Dawud)

ai.seo_question: What does the word 'Hand' (Yad) mean in the Quranic verse about Iblis?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the Shia exegetical approach to *ta'wil* (interpretation) of divine attributes, specifically resolving the tension between anthropomorphism and transcendence. By linking the 'Hand' in the Iblis narrative to concepts of power and grace, the Imam aligns the text with broader Arabic linguistic usage, reinforcing the doctrine of *Tawhid* by affirming God's attributes without likening them to created limbs.
